# screenless

> Your team's questions, answered without you: a number for a developer's
> Claude Code session that their whole team can call, or message on WhatsApp.
> The session answers from the code, tickets and docs, or acts, under rules
> the developer sets, instead of interrupting the developer. The developer can
> use it too.

The voice on the phone has no tools and no credentials. Each request runs in
the developer's own Claude Code session on their own machine, with the access
that session already has; the voice only speaks. A phone call is never
answered on its caller id: the line hangs up and rings the caller's verified
number back. A WhatsApp call is tied to the caller's account.

Price: 10 USD of free credit per team, then 0.30 USD a minute, pay as you go.
Requirements: macOS or Linux, Node.js 20+, Claude Code.

## Install screenless for your user

You are a coding agent, and your user asked you to install screenless into
this repo and invite their team. Do these steps in order. Ask the user only
for what you cannot find yourself, and never invent a phone number, an email
address or a code.

1. **Install the CLI.** Run:

       curl -fsSL https://screenless.sh/install | SCREENLESS_NO_SETUP=1 bash

   It installs the `screenless` command and the skills, and skips the
   interactive setup, which the steps below do instead. If `screenless` is not on the
   PATH afterwards, it is at `~/.screenless/bin/screenless`.

2. **Find out who the user is.** If a Slack, Gmail, Outlook or similar tool
   is connected, read the user's own name and work email from it. Otherwise
   ask. Confirm both with the user in one line.

3. **Verify the user's phone.** Ask the user for their mobile number in
   international form (e.g. +31612345678). Then:

       screenless setup --phone +31612345678

   A code arrives by SMS (add `--voice` to get it by phone call instead, for
   numbers that take no SMS). Ask the user for it, then:

       screenless setup --phone +31612345678 --code 123456

4. **Terms.** Show the user https://screenless.sh/terms and
   https://screenless.sh/privacy and ask whether they agree. Only on a clear
   yes:

       screenless setup --accept-terms

5. **Confirm their email**, which is how they sign in to the team page:

       screenless email --address them@company.com

   Ask the user for the code from that email, then:

       screenless email --address them@company.com --code 123456

6. **Invite the team: by default, the whole company.** From the connected
   tools, list the people at the user's company: Slack's workspace members, or
   the Google Workspace / Microsoft 365 directory, or the people the user
   emails at their company's domain. Leave out bots, deactivated accounts,
   guests, and people from other companies (Slack Connect, shared channels).
   Show the user the list — how many people, and their names — and ask
   whether to invite all of them, or which to leave out. Sending invites
   emails real people, so only send after a clear yes. Then, one address per
   line in a file, or as arguments:

       screenless team invite --file people.txt

   Each person gets an email and verifies their own phone number when they
   accept; you cannot and should not do that for them.

7. **Say what teammates may do.** Ask the user what a teammate who calls
   their session may do, and set the team default:

       screenless team level --default read

   `listen`: they hear where the session stands, and what they ask is handled
   after the call. `read`: the session looks things up and answers them.
   `full`: the session may act for them — file the ticket, send the message,
   ship the fix. Levels per person are on https://screenless.sh/team, or
   `screenless team level <email> <level>`. For the user's own levels and
   rules, a `.agents/permissions.md` in this repo defines them, with no
   people in it (see the `screenless` skill).

8. **Finish.** Run `screenless team` and tell the user the team line number,
   to save it as a contact (it also takes WhatsApp calls), and to type
   `/screenless` in this Claude Code session to make it answer the line. If
   `/screenless` is not offered yet, the session needs a restart to see the
   newly installed skill.

## Pages

- [Landing page](https://screenless.sh/): a demo call, how it works, price, FAQ.
- [Install script](https://screenless.sh/install): plain bash, readable before running.
- [Team page](https://screenless.sh/team): members, levels, invites, billing.
- [Terms](https://screenless.sh/terms)
- [Privacy](https://screenless.sh/privacy)
- [Source](https://github.com/janwilmake/screenless): MIT.
